normalized.governing_thought: Launch Copilot in Q2 2027 in a Pro plan at $12 more per seat, not a $149 add-on, and plan on about $2.9M of new ARR
executive_summary: Customers value Copilot, but a $149 add-on would bring about $2.5M of new ARR, not $8M (Beta productivity rose 9 percentage points more than in matched accounts; Only 14% bought at $149, against 46% 'likely' in the survey)
Routewise has put AI in its plan, but matching it protects at most about $0.6M of new ARR a year (Win rate against Routewise fell from 44% to 37%, alongside a 20% discount)

A Pro plan at $12 more per seat lifts NRR past 105% in its migration year and keeps margin above 75% (Pro needs about 26% of accounts to move; 33% moved to the 2023 tier; Copilot free in Core would cut gross margin to about 71.9%)

Launching first is worth the two-quarter mobile delay, narrowly: mobile is the bigger churn problem (Mobile reliability is cited in 4.5 times as many churn cases as AI; The delay risks up to $1.1M of ARR; waiting defers $1.44M of Pro revenue)
Launch Pro in Q2 2027 with a usage allowance, restart mobile in Q3 and review at six months (Cap use at about 444 requests per seat a month, with paid overage)

slides.title: Launching Dispatch Copilot
Key questions

claims.claim: Should Brightwork launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027, and with what package and price, to lift NRR from 101% to 105% by 2028 while keeping gross margin at 75% or more?
evidence: Decision maker: CEO Maya Okafor and the executive team, at January 2027 planning

Success criteria: Net revenue retention from 101% to 105% by 2028; Company gross margin at or above 75%; A credible answer to Routewise's AI in contested deals; The mobile app rewrite delayed by no more than two quarters
Out of scope: Building or switching the AI model; Engineering headcount above 60; The price of the Core plan

Sub-questions: 1 Does Copilot create value, and how many customers will pay $149 for it? 2 How much business does Routewise's AI cost us, and what does it mean for packaging? 3 Which package and price lift NRR to 105% and keep gross margin at 75% or more? 4 Is Copilot worth delaying the technician mobile app rewrite by two quarters? 5 How should we launch Pro, and what will tell us it is working?

slides.title: Contents
Routewise's AI raises the cost of waiting, but the deals at stake are worth a third of what sales claims

claims.claim: The win-rate drop is real, but Routewise's discount in the same quarter clouds the cause
evidence: −7 pp change in win rate where Routewise competed, Q1–Q2 to Q3 2026

claims.claim: Even a full recovery of the drop is worth only about $0.6M of new ARR a year
evidence: 3x the sales memo's claim compared with that ceiling

claims.claim: Routewise sells AI inside its plan, so a separate add-on would stand out as a surcharge
evidence: 60% of our qualified opportunities where Routewise competes

slides.title: 2a: Our win rate against Routewise fell after it launched AI, but its 20% first-year discount came in the same quarter

claims.claim: We now win fewer of the deals Routewise contests
evidence: −7 pp
Win rate where Routewise competed: Q1–Q2 2026 0.44; Q3 2026 0.37

claims.claim: Two possible causes arrived together in Q3
evidence: 31% of Q3 lost deals mention AI features in their loss notes (A mention, not the stated reason for the loss; Counts all lost deals, not only Routewise deals)
20% off the first year, offered by Routewise in Q3 (Launched in the same quarter as its AI)
Q3 data cannot separate the two effects
Routewise competes in about 60% of our roughly 2,600 qualified new-customer opportunities a year, about 1,560 deals
Routewise launched AI scheduling, included in its Pro plan, in September 2026; the earlier rate covers two quarters, the later one quarter, and deal counts per period are not in the pack

slides.title: 2b: Winning back the whole win-rate drop would add about $0.6M of new ARR a year, a third of the sales claim

claims.claim: Winning back the whole win-rate drop would add about $0.6M of new ARR a year
evidence: 1,560 opportunities a year with Routewise: 2,600 × 60%
7 pp win rate lost: from 44% to 37%
109 deals a year lost to the drop
$5,878 ARR of a new account: 6.2 seats × $79 × 12
$0.6M new ARR a year if all of it came back

claims.claim: This is a ceiling: it credits AI with the whole drop
evidence: It assumes AI, not the 20% first-year discount, caused the entire fall; the gap could widen if Routewise's AI improves
New customers do not count in NRR; Copilot may also defend the 6% of churn that cites AI, about $0.48M of ARR a year

claims.claim: The sales memo's claim is 3 times this ceiling
evidence: The sales memo's 'a third of lost deals' implies about 328 deals and $1.93M, 3 times this ceiling
The memo treats AI mentions in 31% of loss notes as causes, and applies them to deals lost for any reason

slides.title: 2c: With AI included in Routewise's Pro plan, a $149 add-on would be the only AI surcharge in a contested deal

claims.claim: A $149 add-on would be the only AI surcharge in a contested deal
evidence: Routewise Pro: Included in its Pro plan since September 2026; extra a month not in the briefing pack; AI with no separate line item; The offer we must answer
Brightwork $149 add-on: Separate add-on per account; $149; A surcharge on top of Core; Looks dearer, whatever the plan price
Brightwork Pro: Included in a Pro plan, priced per seat; $74.4; Like-for-like with Routewise Pro; Matches the rival's package at half the add-on's price
Copilot free in Core: Included in Core at no charge; None; AI at no price, as at Routewise; Matches, but earns nothing (3c)
Brightwork Pro: $12 more per seat per month than Core; an average account has 6.2 seats

slides.title: 3a: In its migration year Pro would add about $2.9M of new ARR, enough alone to lift NRR past the 105% target

claims.claim: In its migration year Pro would add about $2.9M of new ARR, enough alone to lift NRR past the 105% target
evidence: New ARR: Pro, 2023 migration rate 2.8873; Pro, half that rate 1.4437; ARR needed for 105% NRR 2.304
60,760 office seats today: 9,800 accounts × 6.2 × 33% moved to the 2023 tier in a year × $144 Pro premium a seat a year: $12 × 12 = $2.9M
NRR increase at the 2023 rate 5 pp ($2.9M ÷ $57.6M ARR)
NRR increase at half that rate 2.5 pp ($1.4M ÷ $57.6M ARR)

claims.claim: Pro clears the gap at the 2023 pace, but not at half of it
evidence: 2023 rate: a base-wide precedent, and the premium grows with seats, so larger accounts pay more
Half that rate: Pro would still add ARR, but NRR would stop short of the 105% target
After the move: the lift is one-off; holding 105% later needs lower churn (4a)

slides.title: 3a: Pro misses the NRR gap only if migration runs a fifth below the 2023 pace; the add-on has almost no room

claims.claim: Pro: break-even sits well below the 2023 precedent
evidence: Share of accounts moving to Pro: Needed for 105% NRR 0.2633; Moved to the 2023 tier 0.33

claims.claim: Add-on: break-even sits almost at the volunteer rate
evidence: Share buying the add-on: Needed for 105% NRR 0.1315; Bought in the paywall test 0.14
the paywall's 17 of 120 accounts is too small a sample to tell 13% from 14%

claims.claim: The 33% comes from another tier at another price, so Pro's fifth of headroom is the margin for that doubt
evidence: Gap: NRR from 101% to 105% on $57.6M of ARR, about $2.3M of new ARR; Pro earns $144 a seat a year on 60,760 seats, the add-on $1,788 an account a year on 9,800 accounts

slides.title: 3b: A flat $149 add-on attracts the heaviest users, whose inference can eat most of the price

claims.claim: Buyers self-select into the costly end
evidence: Inference cost per account, $ per month: Median beta account 17.1; Mean beta account 32.4; Paywall buyers 61.2; Top 10% of accounts 130.5; Add-on price 149
41.1% of the $149 price goes to inference for the average buyer
Paywall buyers: used about 1.9 times the requests of the mean beta account
Top 10% of accounts: inference would take about 88% of a $149 price
Median account: cheap to serve, but the least likely to pay a flat fee
The top 10% of beta accounts generated 58% of all AI requests; inference at $0.009 per request is fixed through December 2027

slides.title: 3b: Priced per seat, Pro spends about a third of its premium on inference and can cap heavy use with an allowance

claims.claim: Pro spends about a third of its premium on inference
evidence: 444.4 requests per seat a month: beta mean of 3,600 ÷ 8.1 seats
× $9 inference per thousand requests at $0.009 each = $4 inference per seat a month
÷ $12 Pro premium per seat a month = 33.3% of the premium goes to inference

claims.claim: An allowance at today's mean keeps that share fixed
evidence: Include about 444 requests per seat a month in Pro, the beta mean per seat
Charge overage at $36 or more per thousand requests, the price that holds a 75% margin on extra use
Per-seat pricing grows with the account, unlike a flat $149 per account
If Pro drew heavy users like the paywall buyers, inference would take about 63% of the premium; the allowance is what prevents it (backup)
Inference is fixed at $0.009 per request through December 2027; list prices fell 35% in the past year

slides.title: 3c: Copilot free in Core would cut company gross margin to about 71.9%, below the floor the plan sets

claims.claim: Copilot free in Core would cut company gross margin to about 71.9%
evidence: $57.6M ARR, unchanged: nothing new is sold
− $16.2M cost of revenue: $12.67M today, $2.92M inference for every seat, $0.6M platform
= $41.4M gross profit ÷ $57.6M ARR = 71.9% company gross margin

claims.claim: Only packages that charge for Copilot keep margin above the floor
evidence: Even at the beta median of 1,900 requests per account, margin would be about 74.3%, still under 75%
Pro keeps margin at about 76.5% and the add-on at about 76.2%: new revenue carries the inference
A further 35% cut in inference prices after 2027 would still leave free-in-Core at about 73.7% (backup)
A free tier capped at about 172 requests per seat a month would hold 75%, but adds no ARR and allows under two-fifths of today's mean use

slides.title: Next steps

normalized.recommendation: Launch Copilot in Q2 2027 in a Pro plan at $12 more per seat, not a $149 add-on, and plan on about $2.9M of new ARR. Launch Pro in Q2 2027 with a usage allowance (about 444 requests per seat a month, with paid overage at $36 or more per thousand requests), restart mobile in Q3 and review at six months. Offer Pro to the 240 beta accounts first, then the base at renewal; lead with Pro in every deal Routewise contests. Hold the mobile date: the case holds only if the 14 engineers return to mobile in Q3 2027.

alternatives_considered.treatment: Reject: no room for error, heavy users eat the price. Sized on paywall take-up it brings about $2.5M of new ARR, not $8M; break-even take-up 13.2% sits almost at the 14% volunteer rate; under $1M gross profit a year; pays back in about 21 months; would be the only AI surcharge in a contested deal.
Launch: clears the gap and matches Routewise. About $2.9M new ARR at the 2023 migration rate, needs 26.3% take-up, keeps margin at about 76.5%, pays back in about 13 months.
